summary: Intermittent stream cut during mobile background/network change splits fenced code block; client parser errors and reconnect loop
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that when their iOS app is backgrounded and then resumes on a different network (cellular ↔ wifi), long streaming responses occasionally get cut mid-fenced-code-block (```), producing an incomplete code fence in the first socket, then a short reconnect followed by a duplicate system message. The customer-side parser treats the first fragment as a terminal response (invalid/incomplete markdown) and kicks into a reconnect loop, creating repeated short sessions and duplicate metadata messages in the transcript.

Impact:
- ClipprAI production users intermittently lose the last code block of long streaming responses (affects user-visible content, causes corrupted examples and failed code execution workflows).
- Client side experiences repeated reconnects leading to increased request volume and higher cost for the customer.

Environment:
- Customer: ClipprAI (dedicated tenant)
- Mobile app: iOS 17.4, SDK v1.8.1 (client uses builtin websocket fallback)
- Backend: Redwood hosted API in us-west-2, routing through customer's corporate edge proxy (FastEdge) and our api-gateway -> serving-runtime pool on g4dn-equivalent nodes

Steps to reproduce (customer-supplied):
1) Start a streaming generation (long response containing fenced code blocks > 3000 tokens) from ClipprAI mobile app on wifi.
2) Background the iOS app for ~30s.
3) Switch to cellular network and foreground the app (socket reconnect performed by SDK).
4) Observe that the client receives an early short stream (ends mid-``` fence) then reconnects and receives a second short stream with duplicate system metadata and the remainder of the textual content. Client logs show parser exception and then automatic retry.

Observed behavior:
- First websocket chunk ends with an incomplete triple-backtick fence and then a socket close initiated by upstream (edge proxy emits FIN).
- Second connection returns overlapping prefix tokens and a repeated system role message before the remaining tokens. Transcript contains duplicated system metadata entries and an incomplete code fence in the first session.
- Client parser shows error: "Unterminated fenced code block at EOF"; app retries the request automatically, leading to multiple short sessions.

Expected behavior:
- Either the original stream should be kept open across the network handover, or the client should receive a clean terminal marker and not a mid-codeblock cut. Reconnect path should present a single coherent transcript without duplicated system metadata.

Logs & evidence attached by customer (pasted):
- Client socket trace excerpts (timestamps normalized):
  [2026-03-09T16:12:31Z] WS_RECEIVE: {"delta":"function example(){console.log('hello'","role":"assistant"}\n"}")
  [2026-03-09T16:12:31Z] WS_CLOSE: FIN from upstream
  [2026-03-09T16:12:32Z] WS_OPEN: reconnected
  [2026-03-09T16:12:32Z] WS_RECEIVE: {"delta":"');}\n"}
- Edge proxy (customer) reports a transient TCP FIN during active connection handoff when NAT mapping flips.
- From our side, api-gateway trace shows a short 499-like termination on the original connection and a new request started with identical request-id prefix and explicit system role insertion.

Initial hypothesis:
- FastEdge (customer side) is aggressively closing/refusing half-open sockets during client NAT rebind which causes a partial delivery. api-gateway currently treats that as a clean end-of-stream and emits the session terminal metadata, leading the SDK to consider the message complete even though markdown is syntactically incomplete. When the SDK reconnects it seeds a fresh session which replays system metadata, producing duplicates.

Work completed so far:
- Support replayed the customer's socket logs to confirm mismatch and collected api-gateway traces for the time window.
- SRE ran a short capture of connection churn in us-west-2 and confirmed several FIN/RESET events correlated with IP churn in the same minute window.

Next steps / proposed actions:
1) SRE to add additional logging at api-gateway to capture "last-frame-type" and whether connection termination was from upstream (edge) vs. internal (our worker). (ETA: 2026-03-13)
2) Engineering to evaluate whether api-gateway should treat abrupt FINs during an in-progress stream as "transient path change" and mark session as resumable (avoid emitting terminal metadata until we see canonical end marker). (ETA: 2026-03-16)
3) Support to advise customer on short-term mitigations: increase client-side reconnect backoff, and enable SDK option "prefer-long-lived-socket" to avoid immediate retries. (Suggested patch: client v1.8.2 with backoff change)
4) Customer to test with a bypass of FastEdge (direct mobile -> internet route) to confirm whether proxy is the causal element.

Customer impact notes / business priority:
- ClipprAI is on a dedicated plan and reported this affects >1% of long-run codegen flows during mobile rebinds. They are asking for a short-term config change and timeline for a durable fix.

Attachments:
- client_socket_excerpt.log (customer)
- api_gateway_trace_2026-03-09_16-12.json (support capture)
comments: 2026-03-10 | Support (Leah Park): Opened ticket after customer escalation. Collected initial logs and asked for full client socket dump and the FastEdge proxy config. Recommended customer temporarily disable aggressive connection pruning on their proxy.

2026-03-11 | Customer (J. Morales, ClipprAI): Provided full websocket trace and confirmed they can reproduce reliably when switching from office wifi -> cellular. FastEdge team confirmed a default TCP-mptimeout of 15s and NAT rebind policy. Customer attempted bypass (direct egress) and said issue reduced but not eliminated.

2026-03-11 | SRE (Anika Bose): Captured api-gateway traces for the time window and confirmed FIN/RESET spikes correlated with the customer's request-ids. Proposed adding last-frame-type logging and flagging abrupt upstream terminations. Assigned INT-4210 to track the internal logging change.

2026-03-12 | Eng (Ravi Menon): Reviewing gateway semantics. Preliminary note: we should avoid emitting terminal metadata immediately on upstream FIN if there are indications the stream did not finish syntactically (e.g., unmatched fence). Will prototype a conservative hold-until-idle behavior for 5s.
notes: This ticket is prioritized for the dedicated customer SLA and has cross-team owners (support, SRE, serving runtime).
